lines.text: The task took three hours. Was the agent slow, or was it waiting on you?
The usual guess is that the agent is slow, so maybe it needs a bigger model.
Every task in Agent R Q keeps a timeline of its status, recorded automatically.
Open it, and you get a bar. Working in green, blocked in red, waiting on you in yellow.
Add up the green, and the agent only worked for an hour and twenty five minutes.
Twenty minutes were blocked. The agent hit a wall, like a missing credential, and stopped.
The biggest slice is yellow. An hour and fifteen minutes of approvals, sitting unanswered.
Forty one percent of the task was waiting on a human. Now the bottleneck has a number.
So skip the faster model, and fix the queue instead. Faster approvals, or fewer interruptions.
Pre approve the safe commands once, and that yellow slice shrinks on every task.
Next week, the timeline shows the change. One hour forty, with the agent barely waiting.
Stop guessing why a task was slow. Open the timeline. Try it at Agent R Q dot com.
